⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE
Stateless MCP

Source: blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/2026-07-28/

Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
⚠️ BREAKING CHANGE
Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR)
Replaces server-initiated elicitation/create, sampling/createMessage, and roots/list (SEP-2322)
server responds 
"result": {
  "resultType": "input_required",
  "inputRequests": {
    "github_login": {
      "method": "elicitation/create",
      "params": { ... }
    }
  },
  "requestState": "AEAD-protected blob"
}
client retries with a new id 
"method": "tools/call",
"id": 2,
"params": {
  ...,
  "inputResponses": {
    "github_login": { "action": "accept", ... }
  },
  "requestState": "AEAD-protected blob"
}

No longer requires long-held connections.

Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
Stateless everywhere

Before · stateful (SSE)

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant LB as Load Balancer (sticky)
  participant A as Instance A
  C->>LB: tools/call
  LB->>A: routed, session pinned to A
  A-->>C: server-initiated elicitation/create
pushed down a held-open stream
  Note over A: A holds the in-flight call
and the open stream
  C-->>A: elicitation result, which must reach A
  A-->>C: tool result
  Note over LB,A: Needs sticky routing or shared storage.
Lose the stream and the call is lost

After · MRTR

sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant C as Client
  participant S as Server (any instance)
  C->>S: tools/call (id 1)
  S-->>C: InputRequiredResult (id 1)
resultType input_required + requestState
  Note over S: Request ends here.
Nothing is held in server memory
  C->>U: prompt for the requested input
  U-->>C: answers
  C->>S: tools/call (id 2) + inputResponses + requestState
  Note over S: Any instance. State arrives in the
echoed blob, which is untrusted input
  S-->>C: Result (id 2)
Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
⚠️ DEPRECATION
DCR is deprecated in favour of CIMD
With Client ID Metadata Documents the client_id is an HTTPS URL the client controls (SEP-2352)

BENEFITS · CIMD

No registration step

One client_id works at every AS that supports CIMD.

Identity is verifiable

Domain control backs the client's identity.

Updates propagate

Every AS reads the new metadata on its next fetch.

DRAWBACKS · DCR

A row per client, per server

Each client gets a minted, non-portable client_id.

Registrations outlive the client

Stale client records accumulate silently.

Anyone can register

The consent-screen name and logo are attacker-supplied.

Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
DCR vs CIMD

DCR (RFC 7591)

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as MCP Client
  participant AS as Authorization Server
  C->>AS: GET authorization server metadata (RFC 8414)
  AS-->>C: metadata incl. registration_endpoint
  C->>AS: POST /register (client_name, redirect_uris)
  Note over AS: AS writes a client record,
one row per client, per AS
  AS-->>C: client_id (+ client_secret)
  Note over C,AS: The minted client_id is local:
it isn't portable to another AS
  C->>AS: /authorize?client_id=(minted)
  AS-->>C: consent screen shows self-asserted client_name

CIMD (draft)

sequenceDiagram
  participant C as MCP Client
  participant M as Metadata URL (client-hosted)
  participant AS as Authorization Server
  Note over C,M: Client already hosts metadata JSON at a
stable HTTPS URL, and that URL is the client_id
  C->>AS: /authorize?client_id=https://client.dev/oauth/metadata.json
  Note over AS: client_id is a URL, so fetch it.
No registration record is written
  AS->>M: GET the client_id URL
  M-->>AS: client_id, client_name, client_uri, redirect_uris
  Note over AS: 200 only, no redirects followed.
Document client_id MUST equal the URL
  AS-->>C: consent screen shows fetched client_name

03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
Smaller changes

Header-based routing

Streamable HTTP requests now carry Mcp-Method and Mcp-Name headers, so gateways, rate limiters, and WAFs route and meter without parsing JSON bodies (SEP-2243). We'll use this in the agentgateway lab.

Cacheable list results

tools/list, prompts/list, resources/list, and resources/read responses include ttlMs and cacheScope, enabling deterministic ordering and stable prompt caches across reconnects (SEP-2549).

Issuer validation

Authorization servers must return the RFC 9207 iss parameter and clients must validate it before code redemption, closing a mix-up attack class (SEP-2468).

Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
Tasks
Async tool calls, now an official extension (SEP-2663)

Async tool calls

A call can return a task instead of a result; the client polls tasks/get and picks up the result when it's ready.

Client signals, server decides

The client signals task support on the request; the server decides whether to run the call as a task.

One stream for updates

io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks replaces HTTP GET notifications with a single subscriptions/listen stream.

Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
Deprecations
Deprecated features sunset after 12 months (SEP-2577)

Roots, Sampling, Logging

The server-initiated versions are deprecated; MRTR carries the same interactions as answered requests.

HTTP+SSE transport

The legacy transport is deprecated in favour of Streamable HTTP.

Dynamic Client Registration

Deprecated in favour of CIMD. Existing registrations keep working during the offramp.

All four Tier 1 SDKs (TypeScript, Python, Go, C#) already ship 2026-07-28 support; the Rust SDK is in beta.
Agentic AI Foundation
03 · MCP SPEC
aaif.io / events
The next five priority areas

blog.modelcontextprotocol.io/posts/mcp-roadmap/

Agent identity and enterprise-ready security

Standardised mechanisms for agents running as cloud workloads to be recognised and trusted, moving beyond browser-based authorization. Near term: DPoP and Workload Identity Federation.

Agentic messaging primitives

Extending MCP beyond request-response to support longer-running loops, server-pushed results, and mid-flight work steering.

HTTP-native transport unification

Remote MCP servers as standard HTTP workloads, with local deployment modes unified under a single transport.

PART 3

Enterprise Managed Authentication.

Centrally managed MCP access

Agentic AI Foundation
05 · EMA & AUTH
aaif.io / events
PART 3 · EMA
No more users authorizing apps

TODAY · THE USER DECIDES

An employee wires an MCP server into their agent, hits a consent screen, and clicks approve. That click is the whole access-control decision.
  • — Grants live per user, per server — nobody has the list
  • — Offboarding doesn't reach them
  • — Seeing any of it means a proxy or an L7 firewall in the path

WITH EMA · THE ENTERPRISE DECIDES

The IdP already knows who this person is and what they may reach. ID-JAGs let it say so to an MCP server, so access is granted and revoked where identity already lives.
  • — Admins authorize MCP access, not end users
  • — One place to audit and to cut off
  • — No change to MCP token endpoints; minimal change to the AS
